newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates firm in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates firm in liquid market.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates remained at an average of 10.03125 percent on Friday but touched a low of 10 percent after the Central Bank again closed its overnight borrowing facility, traders said.

"It (the Central Bank) opened for a little while and closed it. So banks had no choice but to lend to each other," a dealer said. The Central Bank had done the same thing on Thursday, saying it had already squared its positions.
Market volume fell to 6.865 billion from 10.179 billion pesos, marked by 21 lenders and 18 borrowers.
"Everybody is cautious right now, waiting for Central Bank's next move. It didn't change its overnight rate but it closed its overnight borrowing facility," a big bank dealer said.
Thus, banks didn't see active positioning in the secondary market, traders said. There were buyers of short-term bills just to meet corporate requirements, they said.
Banks, however, were more interested in buying the one-year bills where rates were higher than the Central Bank's, they said.
A Reuter poll of six financial institutions gave bid rates of 10.625 to 10.50 on the one-year bills.
